(9) Ibn ʿAbbās said: The following individuals once gathered after sunset behind the Kaʿbah: ʿUtbah and Shaybah sons of Rabīʿah, Abū

Sufyān b. Ḥarb, a man from Banī ʿAbd al-Dār, Abū al-Bakhtarī from Banī Asad, al-Aswad b. al-Muṭṭalib, Zamʿah [Rabīʿah] b.

al-Aswad, al-Walīd b. al-Mughīrah, Abū Jahl b. Hishām, ʿAbdAllāh b. Abī Umayyah, Umayyah b. Khalaf, al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, and Nabīh and Munabbih2 sons of al-Ḥajjāj al-Sahmī. They told one another, “Send someone to Muḥammad to talk to him and argue against him so that he may have no more excuse against you.”

They sent a message to him saying, “Indeed the heads of your tribe have gathered to talk to you.” The Messenger of God hastened toward them as he thought that perhaps they have changed

their mind, for he was very eager toward them, he wanted their rectitude, and their misguidance was grievous to him. He came and sat with them.

They said, “O Muḥammad! We have called you in order to leave no more excuse for you. By God we do not know any man from Arab having done to his tribe what you have done to yours. You have indeed cursed our fathers, disapproved our religion, accused our wits of folly, cursed our gods and divided our community.

There is no evil that you have not done to us. If you have come up with this in order to acquire wealth, then we will raise money for you and make you the wealthiest among us. If you want mastery over us, then we will make you our master. If you want kingdom, then we will make you a king over us. If you do what you do because of a jinn that you see and overcomes you, then perhaps we can spend our wealth trying to find a cure for you so that you may be freed from this jinn, and thus leave you no more excuse.”

The Messenger of God replied, “What you said does not apply

than us. So ask your Lord—that has sent you with what He has sent you—to move these mountains that have constricted us away from us, expand our town, flow rivers in it like the rivers in Syria and Iraq, and raise our fathers back to life. Among those who He resurrects there must be Quṣayy b. Kilāb, for he was a truthful old man and we can ask him whether what you are saying is true or false. If you do what we ask you and he confirms

The Messenger of God said, “I have not been sent to do such things. I have come to you from God only by that which He has sent me, and I have conveyed to you what I have been sent with.

Now, if you accept what I have brought for you then that will be your gain in this world and the hereafter, and if you return it back to me then I will wait for God’s command, until God judges between me and you.”

They said, “If you do not do that for us, then choose one of the following for yourself if you are really a messenger as you claim: Ask your Lord to send an angel to confirm what you are saying and turn us away from you. Or ask Him to give you gardens, treasures and palaces of gold and silver that would make you solvent of your current condition that we see, because you go to the market and seek your livelihood just like us. Then we would know your position with your Lord.”

The Messenger of God said, “I am not the person who does so.

I am not a person who would ask his Lord these things. I have not been sent to you for these matters, but God has sent me as a bearer of glad tiding and warning. Now, if you accept what I have brought for you then that will be your gain in this world and the hereafter, and if you return it back to me then I will wait for God’s command, until God judges between me and you.”

They said, “Then cause the heaven to come down upon us, just as you say that your Lord would do if He wills, because we will never believe in you unless you do this.” The Messenger of God said, “That is up to God to do this to you if He wills.”

They said, “O Muḥammad! [If you are truly God’s messenger]

your Lord would have known that we will sit with you, ask you about what we asked, and request from you what we requested.

So He would have sent to you and taught you what would turn us away from you beforehand. He would have informed you of what He shall do to us if we do not accept what you have brought to us. Indeed we have been told that there is this man in Yamāmah named al-Raḥmān who teaches you, but by God we will never ever believe in al-Raḥmān. We have lefiiyou no excuse, O Muḥammad. By God we will not let you go away with what you have done to us unless either we or you are destroyed.” One of them added, “We will never believe in you unless you bring Allah and the angels face to face (with us) (17:92).”

When they said this the Messenger of God got up to leave. Then ʿAbd-Allāh b. Abī Umayyah also got up and said, “O Muḥammad!

Your people offered you what they offered, but you did not accept it from them. Then they asked you certain things by which they may know your position with God, but you did not do it for them.

Then they asked you to bring about the punishment by which you threaten them. By God I will never believe in you unless you take a ladder and ascend to the heaven in front of my eyes, then you come down and bring with you a book that is wide open, along with four angels that would testify that you are what you claim to be. By God even if you do this I do not think I would believe in you.”

Then he lefiithe Messenger of God and the Messenger of God went back to his family in sorrow. Their defiance disappointed him of the hope that he had in them when they had called him.
